Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks for a productive call today. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Pain observed: intermittent 5xxs from our hosted endpoint (502/504) when hitting reranker + structured output tool calling in your workflow. Failures are more frequent under burst load and with requests that include the reranker/embedding step.
- Hypotheses we discussed: auth header mismatch from a short-lived proxy, routing fallback exercising a model variant that doesn't support your tool schema, and a request payload case with deeply nested JSON causing schema validation to trip.

Agreed next steps:
1) You (Tom) to share the request trace + a minimal failing payload (if possible) — Tom mentioned he would attach a trace from the 12:02pm failure.
2) We'll loop in engineering to attempt a repro in staging and return a short playbook (repro steps + temporary mitigations). Alex -> Marissa / Priyom to own.
3) Schedule a 45min debug session Monday to pair on a live repro (please propose times).
4) If short-term mitigation required, we'll propose timeout tuning + a routing fallback to a smaller compatible model while we triage the root cause.

Attachments: session-recording-20261212.mp4 (call recording).

Tom / Elena — please add any missing items and confirm the Monday window.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + action items: Leela Health SDK auth / routing repro — repro steps + quick mitigations

Alex / Priyom / Elena / Tom — I pulled the trace and reproduced a failing case in staging. Notes and a short playbook below.

What I reproduced:
- When the incoming request drops Authorization into X-Forwarded-Authorization we were not normalizing that header before the router auth check in the legacy routing path. Result: intermittent auth failures during bursts where the proxy sometimes forwards Authorization and sometimes X-Forwarded-Authorization.
- For requests that hit the primary model variant that enforces strict tool_calling schema checks, we saw schema validation errors for deeply nested arrays in one of their tool arguments (the reranker wrapper sends an embeddings vector array that occasionally has an extra nested array wrapper due to a client-side marshalling bug). That mismatch causes an early 4xx in the model adapter path for some variants and a 502 if the validation surfaces during batch reduction.

Repro-playbook (attached: repro-playbook.md) — highlights:
1) Example curl to repro auth header mismatch:
   curl -s -H "X-Forwarded-Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @leela-minimal-payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

2) SDK repro (JS):
   const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, normalizeAuthHeaders: true });
   await client.generate({ model: 'redwood/omm-1', input: jsonPayload });

3) Quick mitigations to pass to customer:
   - Short-term: set SDK flag normalizeAuthHeaders=true (we can ship a tiny patch to older SDKs if needed) and increase request timeout to 45s.
   - Routing fallback: configure route override to prefer .redwood/light-3b for the problematic endpoint until we push a fix (routing-policy: fallback_on_schema_error).
   - Client fix: ensure embeddings arrays are flattened to a single vector per item (we include a small snippet in the playbook).

4) Long-term fix items (we'll work on these with infra):
   - Normalize X-Forwarded-Authorization globally at the edge.
   - Harden model adapter batching to avoid 502s on schema-validation failures (make them return structured 4xx where possible).

I can be on the debug call Monday at 10:00 PST. If we want to be safe for their burst pattern, recommend enabling routing fallback + SDK header normalization as a short-term step before our patch lands.

Attaching repro-playbook.md with commands and a minimal payload.

—Marissa Cole
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: repro-playbook.md (text/markdown)]
